The AI All-You-Can-Eat Buffet Is Ending with Gary Marcus | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 62

Eisman maps AI beneficiaries, software risks, financing concentration and physical bottlenecks before interviewing Gary Marcus. Marcus accepts useful coding and brainstorming while emphasizing reliability limits, tool-driven progress and uncertain unit economics. Eisman questions profitable demand rather than treating failure to achieve AGI as sufficient evidence of a bubble, and declines an immediate short despite concern. Several supporting claims require correction or restraint, especially CPU ratios, automatic private-valuation losses and speculation about Anthropic's compute discount.

YouTube · 2026-06-01 ↗Substack · 2026-06-01 ↗
Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

How he reasons here

  • Separate useful specialized AI from AGI claims.
  • Analyze a model together with its tools and verification environment.
  • Trace revenue, compute cost, funding and customer concentration separately.
  • Differentiate announced capacity from paid utilization.
  • A bubble thesis needs a mechanism and catalyst, not just high spending.
  • Test price elasticity when subsidized usage becomes metered.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • AI supply-chain map.
  • Hyperscaler capex and free cash flow.
  • CPU/GPU architecture and power constraints.
  • Token and agent cost accounting.
